name: Sweden
tagline: Free for EU students, but few bachelor's are in English
summary: Sweden has one national application portal, one national ranking system, and no tuition fees for EU/EEA citizens. Your IB total is converted to a Swedish merit value on a published table, and that number alone decides most places - there is no personal statement and usually no interview. The catch is supply: most Swedish bachelor's degrees are taught in Swedish, so the English-taught list is short and the competition on it is national.
whyConsider: No tuition fee at all if you are an EU/EEA or Swiss citizen.
One application at universityadmissions.se covers every Swedish university.
Your IB points convert to a Swedish merit value on a published, public table - you can work out your own score before you apply.
As a Danish speaker you already meet the Swedish-language entry requirement with Danish Language A at grade 4 or higher, which opens Swedish-taught programmes too.
Admission is score-based and transparent: no essays, no references, no interview for most programmes.
watchOuts: English-taught bachelor's degrees are genuinely scarce. Lund lists ten, KTH lists one. Most English teaching in Sweden is at master's level.

You almost certainly cannot use the January round. University Admissions says applicants without a completed IB Diploma should not apply to the first round, so a May 2027 candidate applies in round two (deadline 15 April 2027).
Housing is a queue system you join years in advance in Stockholm. Register the day you decide Sweden is on your list.
Non-EU students: from 11 June 2026 a study residence permit limits you to 15 hours of paid work per week, and new rules also tighten study-progress requirements.
Stockholm School of Economics also demands an SAT, ACT or ITB-Business score on top of the IB - that is unusual for Sweden and needs a year's notice.

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: No national minimum points figure is published. A full IB Diploma awarded 2021 or later gives general eligibility (grundlaggande behorighet) in its own right; individual Course Results do not.
ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: Specific entry requirements are met subject by subject. Minimum IB grade 4 is normally required, with grade 3 accepted for Biology, Chemistry and Physics at HL and for some Mathematics courses. Published maths mapping: Mathematics: applications and interpretation SL maps to Swedish Matematik 3c; Mathematics: analysis and approaches SL maps to Matematik 4; Mathematics: applications and interpretation HL maps to Matematik 5; Mathematics: analysis and approaches HL maps to Matematik specialisering. Sciences: Physics/Chemistry/Biology SL or HL map to Fysik 2 / Kemi 2 / Biologi 2. History SL/HL maps to Samhallskunskap 1b; Economics or Global politics SL/HL maps to Samhallskunskap 2.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: UHR publishes a fixed conversion table from IB total points to the Swedish merit value (meritvarde) on the 10.00-20.00 scale: 24 = 13.18, 25 = 13.94, 26 = 14.62, 27 = 15.21, 28 = 15.76, 29 = 16.26, 30 = 16.70, 31 = 17.11, 32 = 17.53, 33 = 17.92, 34 = 18.25, 35 = 18.57, 36 = 18.88, 37 = 19.17, 38 = 19.38, 39 = 19.54, 40 = 19.70, 41 = 19.79, 42 = 19.90, 43-45 = 20.00. Up to 2.5 extra merit points (meritpoang) can be added for qualifying courses in modern languages, English and mathematics taken outside the Diploma.
notes: IB English A (HL or SL), English B HL, and English B SL taught in English all meet the higher Swedish English 7 requirement. English B SL taught in a language other than English meets English 6, which is the level needed for general eligibility.

The Swedish-language requirement for Swedish-taught programmes can be met with Language and Literature A or Literature A in Swedish, Danish or Norwegian at HL or SL with grade 4 or higher. Danish A counts.

IB applicants sit in selection group BI if eligible on the Diploma alone. They move into BII if they add Swedish upper-secondary or adult-education courses afterwards. If you retake IB exams you are ranked in BI on the original score and in BII on the improved one.
Unlike other foreign-qualification holders, IB students cannot raise their merit value through Swedish komvux courses - they can only retake within the IB system.
For a May session, ask your IB coordinator to release results to UHR through the IB Result Service. For the May 2026 session the stated date was 5 July; check the equivalent date for May 2027.
Rules differ by award year. The 2021-and-later ruleset is the one that applies to a May 2027 Diploma.

deadlines.label: First admission round opens (autumn 2027)
deadlines.notes: This is the round aimed at international applicants. Most English-taught programmes are only offered here.

deadlines.label: First admission round application deadline
deadlines.notes: University Admissions advises applicants who do not yet have a completed IB Diploma NOT to apply in this round, because results cannot be assessed in time. A May 2027 IB candidate normally cannot use it.

deadlines.label: First round document and application-fee deadline
deadlines.notes: Application fee, fee-exemption documents and all supporting materials due.

deadlines.label: Second admission round opens
deadlines.notes: This is the realistic round for a May 2027 IB candidate. Fewer English-taught programmes are open here.

deadlines.label: Second admission round application deadline
deadlines.notes: Also the final ranking day. Application fee and fee-exemption documents due 23 April; supporting documents due 21 June.

deadlines.label: Second round results published
deadlines.notes: You must reply and accept by 16 July. A second notification follows on 22 July.

deadlines.label: Semester start
deadlines.notes: Date given by Stockholm University; other universities start in late August or early September.

steps: Work out your likely merit value from the UHR conversion table before you shortlist anything, because that number is what actually decides your place.
Check each programme's specific entry requirements and match them against your IB subjects and grades - grade 4 is the normal minimum, grade 3 for HL sciences.
Create an account at universityadmissions.se and rank up to a set number of programme choices in order of preference. Your ranking matters: you are only offered your highest-ranked eligible choice.
Upload your IB transcripts and, if you are an EU/EEA citizen, proof of citizenship so you are exempted from the 900 SEK application fee.
Ask your IB Diploma Programme coordinator to send your final results directly to UHR through the IB Result Service.
Reply to your offer by the stated date or you lose the place - Sweden is strict about this.
Register in a student housing queue in your target city as early as you possibly can, independently of the application itself.
application.selectionNotes: Selection is almost entirely by number. A third or more of places on each programme go to the grade groups (BI/BII), where you are ranked on your converted merit value, and a further share goes to applicants ranked on the Swedish national aptitude test (hogskoleprovet), which is sat in Swedish. IB students normally compete in BI. A small number of programmes - art, design, music, architecture - add portfolios or auditions, and Stockholm School of Economics requires an SAT, ACT or ITB-Business score.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Limited. Lund University lists ten English-taught bachelor's programmes, Jonkoping University lists seven, and KTH lists one. Most Swedish bachelor's degrees are taught in Swedish; English dominates at master's level.
language.englishProof: You need Swedish English 6 / English Level 2. An IB English A (HL or SL), English B HL, or English B SL taught in English exceeds this and meets the higher English 7. English B SL taught in another language meets English 6. Without an IB English course, IELTS Academic 6.5 with no section below 5.5, or TOEFL iBT total 90 with 20 in writing (for results up to 20 January 2026) / total 4.5 on the new 1-6 scale with no section below 4 (for results from 21 January 2026), are accepted.
notes: Swedish-taught programmes need Swedish 3 level. Danish Language A or Literature A at HL or SL with grade 4 satisfies it, which is a real advantage for a Danish IB student.
The national aptitude test (hogskoleprovet), which fills part of every programme's intake, is only available in Swedish.
Everyday life in Swedish cities runs comfortably in English, but municipal paperwork does not always.

tuitionEuEea.value: No tuition fee. Citizens of the EU, EEA and Switzerland are exempt from both the application fee and tuition, but must document their citizenship to get the exemption.

tuitionNonEu.value: Set by each university. Uppsala University states 49,500-90,000 SEK per semester of full-time study, i.e. roughly 99,000-180,000 SEK per year (about EUR 8,800-16,000 at 11.2750 SEK/EUR). Fees vary widely by subject and institution.
tuitionNonEu.year: Uppsala page last updated 9 October 2025; the page does not state an entry year - re-check for 2027 entry

costs.applicationFee: 900 SEK (about EUR 80) per semester applied for, regardless of how many programmes you choose. EU/EEA/Swiss citizens are exempt.

livingCostMonthly.value: Lund University's own student budget: food 3,000 SEK, accommodation 4,000-8,000 SEK, course literature 400-1,000 SEK, other 1,500 SEK - roughly 8,900-12,500 SEK per month (about EUR 790-1,110). Swedish students on full state loans and grants receive roughly 9,000-12,000 SEK per month.

notes: Non-EU students applying for a study residence permit must show at least 10,656 SEK per month (about EUR 945) for the whole permit period if applying in 2026; the 2025 figure was 10,584 SEK. The amount is reset each year.
The study residence permit application itself costs 1,500 SEK (about EUR 133) for adults.
Euro conversions use the ECB reference rate of 11.2750 SEK per EUR on 21 September 2026 and will drift.

funding: Danish SU: Danish students can in many cases take Danish SU abroad for a full degree in the EU/EEA. This is decided by the Danish authorities, not the Swedish ones - check the SU rules yourself, we have not verified the current conditions here.

CSN (the Swedish student finance agency) is the route for those with a settled connection to Sweden; eligibility for an EU citizen who moves purely to study is restricted and must be checked directly with CSN.
Swedish Institute scholarships and individual university scholarships exist mainly for fee-paying non-EU/EEA students. Bachelor-level availability is limited - check each university.
Because there is no tuition fee for EU/EEA citizens, the real cost question in Sweden is rent, not fees.
workRights: EU/EEA citizens can work without restriction alongside study. Non-EU students on a study residence permit granted on or after 11 June 2026 may work a maximum of 15 hours per week. Source: https://www.migrationsverket.se/en/you-want-to-apply/study/higher-education.html
residency: As an EU/EEA citizen you do not need a residence permit for Sweden - you have a right of residence as a student. In practice you register with Skatteverket to get a personnummer, which you need for almost everything from a bank account to a doctor's appointment, and that normally requires an intended stay of at least 12 months. Non-EU citizens must apply to Migrationsverket for a residence permit for higher education studies, showing admission, health insurance for courses under a year, and at least 10,656 SEK per month (2026 figure) for the permit period; the fee is 1,500 SEK.
housing: Not allocated by the universities. Each city has its own student housing foundation with a credit-day queue - SSSB in Stockholm, AF Bostader and LU Accommodation in Lund, SGS in Gothenburg, Uppsalahem in Uppsala. You earn one credit day per day in the queue, so joining early is the whole game; SSSB waits are commonly quoted in the hundreds of days. Most large universities give no housing guarantee. Register in the queue as soon as a city is on your shortlist, well before you apply.
healthcare: As a Danish EU citizen, carry your EU health insurance card for necessary care. Once you register with Skatteverket and get a personnummer you use the normal Swedish system with the usual patient fees. Non-EU students must hold comprehensive health insurance for studies under one year; for longer permits they are normally covered once registered.

institutions.name: Lund University
institutions.englishBachelors: Ten English-taught bachelor's programmes open to international students
institutions.note: The closest big Swedish university to Denmark - about 45 minutes from Copenhagen by train - and the one with the widest English-taught bachelor's list.

institutions.name: Uppsala University
institutions.note: The oldest university in the Nordics, with a student-nation social life that is unlike anywhere else in Scandinavia.

institutions.name: Stockholm University
institutions.note: Strong in social sciences and sits inside a national park in the middle of the capital, though most bachelor teaching is in Swedish.

institutions.name: KTH Royal Institute of Technology
institutions.englishBachelors: One: BSc Information and Communication Technology
institutions.note: Sweden's leading technical university, but at bachelor level it teaches in English on exactly one programme.

institutions.name: Chalmers University of Technology
institutions.englishBachelors: Not verified for bachelor's. Chalmers states that its two-year master's programmes are taught entirely in English; check bachelor-level language before applying.
institutions.note: Sweden's other big engineering school, closely tied to Gothenburg's automotive and maritime industries.

institutions.name: University of Gothenburg
institutions.note: A broad university spread across Sweden's second city, with unusually strong art and design schools attached.

institutions.name: Stockholm School of Economics
institutions.englishBachelors: Two: Business and Economics, and Retail Management
institutions.note: Small, private and very selective: it asks for at least 31 IB points but says 39 or above is usually needed, plus an SAT of 1300, ACT 28 or ITB-Business 112.

institutions.name: Jonkoping University
institutions.englishBachelors: Seven English-taught bachelor's programmes across business, engineering, health and communication
institutions.note: A smaller foundation university in a lakeside town that punches above its weight on English-taught bachelor's, especially through its international business school.

institutions.name: Linkoping University
institutions.note: Known for problem-based, project-heavy teaching and a campus culture built around student-run engineering work.

institutions.name: Umea University
institutions.note: Far north, dark in winter, and home to one of Europe's most respected industrial design schools.

institutions.name: Malmo University
institutions.note: Twenty minutes over the bridge from Copenhagen, young, practical and very international in outlook.

institutions.name: Lulea University of Technology
institutions.note: Arctic-adjacent technical university with a space campus in Kiruna and close ties to Sweden's heavy industry.

institutions.name: Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences
institutions.note: The place to look if you want animals, forests, food systems or landscape rather than a conventional science degree.

institutions.name: Karolinska Institutet
institutions.note: World-famous for medical research and it awards the Nobel Prize in Medicine; check the language of instruction on each bachelor programme page, because we could not confirm it and most Swedish health degrees are taught in Swedish.
